nuclear.data_note: ATB 2025 shows nuclear costs only as charts; values are from NLR's ATB-calc repository, 'a CSV copy of the ATB data workbook XLSX data' (tests/data/Nuclear, updated 2025-04-25, https://github.com/NatLabRockies/ATB-calc/tree/main/tests/data/Nuclear): Moderate scenario, Market case, 30-year cost recovery, 2030 online date (a reactor can't be online by the other technologies' 2027: Moderate construction 82 months). land_acres_per_mw_nuclear.source: DOE Office of Nuclear Energy: 'A typical 1,000-megawatt nuclear facility ... needs a little more than 1 square mile' (640 acres); Sandia SAND2020-12368C gives ~0.83 acres/MW for a 600 MW plant

land_acres_per_mw_nuclear_smr.source: ORNL/TM-2014/300 (DOE SMR siting report): 'most SMR base design packages can be accommodated on a 50 acre footprint' at 360 MW(e); Sandia gives ~0.06 acres/MW for a 600 MW NuScale plant

california_policy.title: California law bars new nuclear power plants
california_policy.detail: Public Resources Code §25524.2 bars a new nuclear plant until the Energy Commission finds a federally approved, demonstrated means of disposing of high-level nuclear waste, and §25524.1 until fuel reprocessing is approved. AB 2647 (Chapter 830, Statutes of 2026) only orders a Commission nuclear assessment by 2028; it doesn't lift the moratorium. A reactor here, large or SMR, would need a change in state law.
california_policy.source: Cal. Public Resources Code §25524.2 (also §25524.1; AB 2647 status: calmatters.digitaldemocracy.org/bills/ca_202520260ab2647)
